newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares up with U.S., flat trade seen ahead.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares up with U.S., flat trade seen ahead.

text.p: Norwegian shares rallied late in the session on Tuesday after the U.S. fourth-quarter employment cost index rose lower than expected.
Oslo's Total share index finished 0.69 percent higher at 1,058.51 points, a record close. Turnover was heavy at 1.1 billion crowns.
"The U.S. figures helped us finish higher," a dealer said. "We will continue to depend on the United States. U.S. interest rates are now the biggest danger to the Norwegian stock market."
The Oslo Bourse has rallied for most of January, rising about 10 percent so far this year.
"We don't expect a major setback but trade will be relatively flat ahead. A lot of the potential has already been exploited and we have to expect more quiet times," one dealer said.
Forestry group Norske Skog A shares closed 2.78 percent up at 203.50 crowns in what could be a correction after being weak for some time. The forestry index in neighbouring Sweden rose.
Energy company Hafslund's A share was the most traded of the session at 293 million crowns, rising 2.46 percent to 50 crowns. Dealers said a big block of shares in Hafslund changed hands.
